definitions.explanation: The act of committing a crime, or a crime that has been committed. A formal legal and literary term used in judicial and historical contexts.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{罪犯|ざいはん}は{重|おも}い。
{罪犯|ざいはん}の{証拠|しょうこ}が{裁判|さいばん}で{示|しめ}された。
examples.english: Evidence of the criminal act was presented at the trial.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{罪犯|ざいはん}を{悔|く}い{改|あらた}め、{社会|しゃかい}{復帰|ふっき}を{目指|めざ}す{人|ひと}も{少|すく}なくない。
examples.english: There are quite a few people who repent of their past offenses and aim to reintegrate into society.

notes:
Composed of {罪|ざい} (crime, sin, guilt) and {犯|はん} (offense, perpetration). A formal term found in legal documents, historical texts, and literary writing. In everyday language, {犯罪|はんざい} (crime) is the standard term; {罪犯|ざいはん} reverses the character order and carries a more literary or archaic tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罪犯|ざいはん}を{犯|おか}す: to commit an offense
- {罪犯|ざいはん}の{記録|きろく}: record of criminal acts
- {重|じゅう}{罪犯|ざいはん}: serious offense

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {犯罪|はんざい}: crime — the standard, everyday term with reversed character order
- {罪|つみ}: sin, crime, guilt — can be used in both legal and moral senses
- {犯行|はんこう}: criminal act — emphasizes the specific action of committing a crime
